label: churn100-s9
summary: The model predicts churn as a sum of a few readable signals on the logit. The strongest is customer service calls: risk switches on at the third call and climbs with each further call (for the typical customer 3% at two calls, 17% at four, 73% at six); switching that gate off lowers training AUC from 0.892 to 0.803. An international plan adds a step (2.44 on the logit for the 380 holders; typical risk 3% to 27%). Heavy daytime use raises risk past a day-minutes threshold (1030 customers on the gate), and a combined-bill gate raises it when the day charge is high, earlier when the evening charge is also high, while at moderate evening charges the chain cancels the direct evening-charge edge. A direct linear score adds the rest; its largest term is the voice-mail plan (-0.46 per sd), and a Rhode Island state gate lowers risk (-1.65 on the logit in the probe). Two units are dormant on the training data: the voicemail-message gate and a second service-call pathway. The parts add on the logit (self-probe: the service-call and plan contributions are unchanged when the other is switched on), and the decomposition reproduces the model to 4.4e-16.
